title: RevocationChecker default skip is a pit of failure for custom impls
description: RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor has a default impl that returns Ok(()) (skip). The trait rustdoc (pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs lines 615-703) warns about this extensively, and pkix-chain's verify_chain rustdoc (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 367-383) documents it again. But the API shape itself is a pit of failure: any custom RevocationChecker that only implements check_revocation() will silently skip the anchor-issued cert with no compile-time or runtime signal. The warning text is thorough, but the damage when someone misses it is a silent security gap (the cert closest to the root is unchecked). What goes wrong: a consumer implements RevocationChecker with only check_revocation(), deploys it, and the cert issued directly by the trust anchor is never revocation-checked. There is no test assertion, no log, no metric — just a silent Ok(()). Consider: (a) a lint or clippy-style check in CI that detects impl RevocationChecker without check_revocation_against_anchor, (b) a sealed helper trait that requires both methods, or (c) a runtime diagnostic on the Verifier that logs when the default is hit. This is an API-contract risk, not a correctness bug in the existing code — CrlChecker and OcspChecker both override correctly.
notes:
Analysis 2026-11-25: confirmed as described, no shipped instance of the gap, and there is a cleaner fix than the three listed. P1 -> P2; the remaining decision is a release call.

The bead says "CrlChecker and OcspChecker both override correctly". It undercounts. Audited every RevocationChecker impl in the workspace and ALL SIX real checkers override check_revocation_against_anchor:
- CrlChecker (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:757)
- OcspChecker (pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:287)
- NoCheckShim (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:1602)
- HttpCrlFetcher (pkix-revocation-http/src/crl.rs:140)
- HttpOcspFetcher (pkix-revocation-http/src/ocsp.rs:142)
- CachedHttpCrlFetcher (pkix-revocation-http/src/cache.rs:1055)
- CachedHttpOcspFetcher (pkix-revocation-http/src/cache.rs:1302)

The one impl that does NOT override is NoRevocation (lib.rs:797), where relying on the default is exactly right -- "no revocation checking" is its whole meaning. The default itself sits at lib.rs:772 in a trait starting at :696.

So the exposure is entirely to EXTERNAL custom impls, and the bead is right to call it an API-contract risk rather than a correctness bug.

A fourth option, better than the three listed: make the default FAIL CLOSED. A defaulted method that skips a security check should return an error, not Ok(()). Then a custom impl that forgets the override fails loudly on the first anchor-issued certificate instead of silently passing it, and NoRevocation gains one explicit override stating that skipping is intended. That beats (a) a bespoke CI lint, which only protects this workspace -- where the audit above shows there is nothing to protect; (b) a sealed helper trait, which is breaking AND removes the ability to write a checker at all for callers who legitimately only handle the non-anchor case; and (c) runtime logging, which adds an output channel to a crate that is otherwise quiet and no_std-friendly, and which a deployer who missed the rustdoc will also miss in the logs.

Why I did not just do it: pkix-revocation is 0.4.0 and f55d08e7 released it, so turning a silently-passing default into an erroring one is a behavioural break for any external checker that currently relies on the skip -- precisely the population at risk. That is the same release decision as PKIX-lnnl.4 and belongs to you. Mechanically it is two lines: the default body, and the NoRevocation override.

Related: this is the same shape as the hazard recorded in the forwarding-impls memory -- a defaulted trait method silently changing behaviour for impls that do not know about it. It bit this workspace once already, when the Arc<T> forwarding impl for RevocationCache did not forward the new atomic-put methods.
